name: Marsh Rose
lede: Marsh Rose is a muted, dusty red-brown named for the rose, recorded by the Maerz and Paul dictionary in 1930 with a first use in 1927.

sections.title: A rose, dulled
sections.body:
Our data traces the name to the rose, the flower, rather than a pigment or a place [1]. The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 plots it on plate 4 I9 and gives it a first recorded use of 1927, and the ISCC-NBS system files the same area as "grayish red" [1]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 52, chroma 23, hue 26 degrees: a muted, moderate-dark red leaning brown [1].

Its nearest computed neighbor is [[copper-penny|Copper Penny]], just 2.7 units off and almost the same color, followed by [[copper-rose|Copper Rose]] and [[brick-rose|Brick Rose]] [2]. The closest everyday name is [[mauve]], about 11.1 units away, though the two colors share little beyond that measured distance [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 163, as photographed (59 by the stricter within-painting measure), which makes it more common than 52 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.5 times the expected rate (16 of 721 paintings), and most of the Kalighat school in particular, 5.8 times the baseline [4]. The earliest match is a painting dated to the year 1000, 930 years before the name's first record in 1930; that only shows the hue existed long before anyone wrote it down, not that any pigment did, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4].
